You are an ALTITUDE reviewer for a code-quality pass (not a bug hunt). Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim

Get the diff under review by running: `cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim && git diff HEAD~1..HEAD -- driver tests/andes_sim`

This is the F7 feature: `andes-sim run --model fast` transparent passthrough. New: driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/run_passthrough.{cpp,hpp}. Modified: driver/engine_registry.cpp, driver/main.cpp.

Background — the framework's design philosophy (from driver/ROADMAP.md and docs/engine_interface.md): engines are discovered at runtime and self-describe their `invoke` templates per role (standalone/fast-leg/accurate-leg); the framework keeps "zero per-engine code" — everything it needs comes from the descriptor. F8 (`run --model accurate`, Verilator-only) and F9 (`run --model hybrid`) are coming next and will share this `run` command and the passthrough mechanism.

Your angle — ALTITUDE: Check each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile special-case bandaid on shared infrastructure. Special-casing where generalizing would be cleaner is the smell.

Specific things worth checking (read cmd_run.cpp, run_passthrough.{cpp,hpp}):
- run_passthrough.{cpp,hpp} hardcode no engine knowledge — good. But does cmd_run's `run_fast` special-case qemu in a way that F8's `run_accurate` will have to copy-paste (engine resolve + role="standalone" + passthrough)? Is `fast` vs `accurate` really just "resolve engine X, role standalone, exec passthrough"? Could a single `run_standalone(model, default_engine_id, role)` serve both, so F8 is a one-line addition rather than a parallel copy? Or is that premature now (only fast exists)?
- The "engine must be 'qemu'" guard and the qemu-only resolution: is binding fast->qemu at the right layer, or should the model->engine default mapping live in models.hpp (which already lists each model's engine composition)?
- Is putting the qemu `standalone` invoke template as a hardcoded literal in builtin_qemu() the right altitude, given verilator engines self-describe their standalone template via --describe?

Be careful NOT to over-engineer: flag a generalization only if it removes a real, imminent duplication (F8 is genuinely next) or a fragile special-case — not speculative future-proofing. For each finding: `file:line`, one-line `summary`, the concrete cost (fragility / imminent copy-paste), and the deeper form. Distinguish "do now" from "note for F8". Do not hunt for correctness bugs. Return a concise findings list (or "no findings").

1	// The three models andes-sim composes from engines. A model says *which*
2	// engines run and *how* they combine; the concrete engine(s) are resolved
3	// separately (built-in qemu, or a discovered verilator:<cfg>).
4	//
5	//   fast      = QEMU alone (functional), transparent passthrough.
6	//   accurate  = one Verilator alone, pure from reset, transparent passthrough.
7	//   hybrid    = QEMU fast-forwards, Verilator measures the ROI (+ a trigger).
8	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_MODELS_HPP
9	#define ANDES_SIM_MODELS_HPP
10	
11	#include <string_view>
12	
13	namespace andes_sim {
14	
15	struct Model {
16	  std::string_view name;
17	  std::string_view engines;  // engine composition, for `list models`
18	  std::string_view notes;
19	};
20	
21	inline constexpr Model kModels[] = {
22	    {"fast", "qemu", "functional; transparent passthrough"},
23	    {"accurate", "verilator:<cfg>",
24	     "cycle-accurate, pure from reset; transparent passthrough"},
25	    {"hybrid", "qemu -> verilator",
26	     "QEMU fast-forwards, Verilator measures the ROI; pick "
27	     "--trigger csr|pc|icount|simpoint"},
28	};
29	
30	inline const Model* find_model(std::string_view name) {
31	  for (const Model& m : kModels)
32	    if (m.name == name) return &m;
33	  return nullptr;
34	}
35	
36	}  // namespace andes_sim
37	
38	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_MODELS_HPP

1	// andes-sim command-line parsing.
2	//
3	// The grammar is deliberately tiny and stable across all subcommands:
4	//
5	//   andes-sim <cmd> [--model M] [--engine E] [--trigger T] [positional...]
6	//                   [-- <verbatim engine args...>]
7	//
8	// The single most important rule is the `--` boundary: every token after the
9	// first `--` is captured verbatim into `passthrough` and is NOT interpreted by
10	// the framework. That is what lets `fast`/`accurate` forward an engine's whole
11	// native CLI (e.g. `-gdb tcp::1234 -S`) untouched, so users see one simulator.
12	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
13	#define ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP
14	
15	#include <string>
16	#include <vector>
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	struct Cli {
21	  std::string subcommand;                 // e.g. "run", "list"; "" if none
22	  std::string model;                      // --model fast|accurate|hybrid
23	  std::string engine;                     // --engine <id>
24	  std::string trigger;                    // --trigger csr|pc|icount|simpoint
25	  std::string what;                       // --what <target> (build)
26	  std::vector<std::string> positional;    // non-flag framework args
27	  std::vector<std::string> passthrough;   // verbatim, everything after `--`
28	  bool help = false;                      // -h / --help (before `--`)
29	  bool dry_run = false;                   // --dry-run (build, run, test, ...)
30	  bool has_passthrough = false;           // a `--` boundary was present
31	  std::string error;                      // non-empty => parse failed
32	};
33	
34	// Parse argv[1..] (program name skipped). The vector overload is the testable
35	// core; the argv overload adapts it for main().
36	Cli parse_cli(const std::vector<std::string>& args);
37	Cli parse_cli(int argc, char** argv);
38	
39	}  // namespace andes_sim
40	
41	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_CLI_HPP

1	# Engine interface
2	
3	How a simulator joins the `andes-sim` framework.
4	
5	`andes-sim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
6	one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu`, `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`,
7	`verilator:ax66_makatau`, and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`,
8	`sid`, or anything else. Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
9	the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andes-sim` needs to
10	know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
11	zero per-engine code in the framework.
12	
13	To join, an engine does two things:
14	
15	1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
16	2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
17	   (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
18	   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that
19	   only ever runs standalone needs none of this.
20	
21	## 1. The `--describe` JSON
22	
23	Running `<engine-binary> --describe` must print one JSON object to **stdout**
24	and exit 0. Example (Verilator):
25	
26	```json
27	{
28	  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
29	  "type":     "verilator",
30	  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",
31	  "vlen":     512,
32	  "xlen":     64,
33	  "triggers": ["csr", "pc", "icount"],
34	  "roles":    ["standalone", "accurate-leg"],
35	  "state":    ["resume", "drain"],
36	  "invoke": {
37	    "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
38	    "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
39	                     "--handoff-out", "{state_out}", "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}"]
40	  },
41	  "result":   "stderr:cycles"
42	}
43	```
44	
45	### Fields
46	
47	| Field      | Type            | Required | Meaning |
48	|------------|-----------------|----------|---------|
49	| `id`       | string          | yes      | Unique engine id. Convention: `verilator:<cfg>`, `alioth`, `sid`. First id wins on a collision. |
50	| `type`     | string          | yes      | Family: `qemu` \| `verilator` \| `alioth` \| `sid` \| ... |
51	| `kind`     | string          | no       | `functional` or `cycle-accurate`. Shown by `list engines`. |
52	| `vlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `VLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
53	| `xlen`     | number          | no       | 32 or 64. |
54	| `triggers` | array\<string\> | no       | ROI delimiters the engine understands: `csr` \| `pc` \| `icount`. |
55	| `roles`    | array\<string\> | no       | `standalone` \| `fast-leg` \| `accurate-leg` (see below). |
56	| `state`    | array\<string\> | no       | `hybrid_state_v1` capabilities: `resume`, `drain`. Omit if none. |
57	| `invoke`   | object          | no       | Per-role argv template (see Placeholders). |
58	| `result`   | string          | no       | Where the measurement is: `stderr:<word>` or `state.mcycle`. |
59	
60	The parser is strict JSON (no comments, no trailing commas). Numbers are read
61	as integers. Unknown fields are ignored, so the schema can grow.
62	
63	### Roles
64	
65	- `standalone` -- run a whole program alone (the `fast` and `accurate` models).
66	  Transparent passthrough: `andes-sim` forwards the user's post-`--` args
67	  verbatim and the engine's own stdout/stderr/exit code is the result.
68	- `fast-leg` -- the QEMU fast-forward leg of a `hybrid` run: execute up to the
69	  ROI entry, then **drain** `hybrid_state_v1`.
70	- `accurate-leg` -- the cycle-accurate leg of a `hybrid` run: **resume** from a
71	  drained state, execute the ROI, then **drain** again. Its `mcycle` delta is
72	  the reported cycle figure.
73	
74	### invoke + placeholders
75	
76	`invoke` maps a role to its argv template. The framework substitutes these
77	tokens when it builds the command:
78	
79	| Placeholder   | Filled with |
80	|---------------|-------------|
81	| `{bin}`       | the engine binary path |
82	| `{elf}`       | the workload ELF |
83	| `{state_in}`  | the input state file (resume) |
84	| `{state_out}` | the output state file (drain) |
85	| `{mmap}`      | the shared-memory backing file |
86	
87	`standalone` typically needs only `["{bin}", "{elf}"]`; the user's `--` args are
88	appended.
89	
90	### result
91	
92	How `andes-sim` reads the measurement when it is NOT draining state:
93	`stderr:cycles` means "scrape the integer next to the word `cycles` from the
94	engine's stderr" (vsim prints `<n> cycles simulated`). `state.mcycle` means the
95	figure is the `mcycle` field of the drained `hybrid_state_v1`.
96	
97	## 2. ABI conformance
98	
99	Any engine listing `resume` or `drain` in `state` must exchange architectural
100	state through `struct hybrid_state_v1` exactly as defined in
101	`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, and the V block;
102	little-endian; `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`). V data registers travel through
103	the shared-memory scratch region by the convention the header documents. An
104	engine that only claims `standalone` (no `state`) is exempt.
105	
106	## Discovery (how the framework finds engines)
107	
108	`andes-sim list engines` performs discovery; every other engine-using command
109	shares it:
110	
111	1. The built-in `qemu` descriptor is always present (QEMU does not implement
112	   `--describe`; its binary path honors `$VSIM_QEMU`).
113	2. The scan directory is:
114	   - `$ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR` if set (colon-separated; **replaces** the default
115	     and accepts **any** executable -- this is where you drop `alioth` / `sid`),
116	   - otherwise `<repo>/verilator/build`, filtered to `sim_*` binaries.
117	3. For each candidate binary the framework runs `<bin> --describe`. If that
118	   fails (non-zero, hang past a 5 s timeout, or non-JSON) it falls back to a
119	   sidecar file `<bin>.json` containing the same descriptor -- the escape hatch
120	   for binaries that cannot add the flag.
121	4. Descriptors are deduped by `id`.
122	
123	Because discovery is pure runtime scan + self-describe, **building a new
124	Verilator config and dropping `sim_<cfg>` into the scan dir makes it appear with
125	no `andes-sim` rebuild.** That is the hot-plug guarantee.
126	
127	## Joining as a new engine (alioth / sid)
128	
129	1. Implement `--describe` to print the JSON above (set `id`, `type`, `kind`,
130	   the roles you support, and `invoke` templates for those roles). If you cannot
131	   add the flag, ship a `<bin>.json` sidecar instead.
132	2. If you claim `resume`/`drain`, read/write `hybrid_state_v1` per
133	   `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
134	3. Put the binary on `$ANDES_SIM_ENGINES_DIR` and run `andes-sim list engines`
135	   to confirm it shows up. Done -- no framework change required.

content.text: Let me look at the existing `find_engine` in run_plan.cpp to compare with cmd_run's copy.

Diff fully reviewed. Two altitude findings, plus explicit "checked, no change" answers to the three posed questions.

## Findings

### 1. Duplicate `find_engine` helper — this diff adds the second copy (do now)
`driver/cmd_run.cpp:20` and `driver/run_plan.cpp:25` are now two byte-identical file-local `find_engine` (linear scan, `e.id == id`, return `&e`); the only difference is the first param spelling (`Discovery&` vs `std::vector<EngineDescriptor>&`, and cmd_run's iterates `disc.engines`).
- **Cost:** engine-lookup-by-id is the framework's most basic registry primitive, and it's now copy-pasted across two of the run/plan command files. F8 (`run_accurate`) and F9 (`run_plan`) both need it, so the copies will keep multiplying.
- **Deeper form:** one shared lookup in `engine_registry.hpp` (free function over `const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>&`, or a `Discovery::by_id`). cmd_run calls `find_engine(disc.engines, "qemu")`. Low-risk, removes a real present duplication, serves every future run mode.

### 2. `run_fast`'s body is a standalone-passthrough spine that F8 will parallel-copy (note for F8)
`driver/cmd_run.cpp:26-63`. `run_fast` = positional validation (missing-ELF / extra-positional, lines 27-39) + per-model engine resolution (guard + resolve, 41-52) + the passthrough tail (`run_passthrough(eng, "standalone", elf, passthrough)` + err handling, 54-61). F8's `run_accurate` (ROADMAP: same file, role standalone, `exec_passthrough`) shares the positional validation and the passthrough tail verbatim; only engine resolution differs.
- **Cost:** imminent copy-paste — F8 is genuinely next and lands in this same function-set. If it clones `run_fast`, the ~12-line validate+passthrough tail and the "exactly one ELF positional" checks diverge across two functions.
- **Deeper form / seam:** the shared part is *validate-positional + passthrough(role="standalone")*; the per-model part is *engine resolution*. A helper `run_standalone(const Cli&, const EngineDescriptor& eng)` (each model resolves `eng`, then calls it) makes F8 ≈ "resolve the sole verilator" + one call.
- **Correction to the proposed signature:** `run_standalone(model, default_engine_id, role)` does **not** cleanly serve both — `fast`'s default engine is the constant `"qemu"`, but `accurate`'s is the *discovered* sole `verilator:<cfg>` (no fixed id; ROADMAP F8 "default = the sole built one"). So engine resolution can't collapse to a static id param; keep it per-model and share only the tail.
- **Do-now vs F8:** defer to F8. Only one caller exists today; building the helper now is a one-caller abstraction (mild over-engineering). The requirement is that F8 *extract* this spine rather than copy `run_fast`.

## Posed questions — checked, no change

**Q: model→engine default mapping into `models.hpp`?** No. `models.hpp:21-28` `kModels[].engines` is free-text for `list models` ("qemu", "verilator:<cfg>", "qemu -> verilator") — not a machine-readable id. More fundamentally, a static table can't express `accurate`/`hybrid`, whose engines are resolved by discovery, not by a constant id. So model→engine resolution rightly lives in `cmd_run`, per-model. The hardcoded `"qemu"` is `fast`'s defining fact and is at the right layer (the `"qemu"` literal recurring ~3x inside `run_fast` is subsumed by finding 2's `eng`-as-local refactor).

**Q: qemu `standalone` invoke template as a hardcoded literal in `builtin_qemu()`?** Correct altitude. `engine_registry.cpp:51-55`. QEMU is built-in *precisely because it has no `--describe`* (documented in `docs/engine_interface.md` and the Discovery section); the pre-existing `fast-leg` literal already set this precedent, and `standalone` is a consistent sibling. The asymmetry vs Verilator self-describing its `standalone` template is inherent, not a smell. The partial overlap between the `standalone` and `fast-leg` templates is readable config data, not worth factoring.

**Q: `run_passthrough.{cpp,hpp}` engine knowledge?** Confirmed zero — engine + role are params, only `{bin}`/`{elf}` substituted, then verbatim args appended. F8's verilator `standalone` (`["{bin}","{elf}"]`) reuses it unchanged. Right altitude.
